source.title: Predicting the Emergence of Induction Heads in Language Model Pretraining
source.authors: Tatsuya Aoyama; E. Wilcox; N. Schneider

record.tranche_reason: Measures induction behavior with prefix-matching score, following the original measurement, and tests its emergence under varied training and data settings.
record.gate_note: The study measures induction-head behavior and its development. Appendix L reports repetition statistics for datasets and tokenizers as a proxy, not model emergence results; those statistics are not rows. The study cites findings from prior work, which are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: Uses the original prefix-matching score, plus logit attribution and associative recall, to track induction-head emergence in GPT2 LMs trained from scratch. It varies batch size, context size, natural bigram repetition, and semi-natural and synthetic data properties. It also covers 6 pretrained Pythia checkpoints. Results bear on V2 (abruptness), V4 (GPT2/Pythia 50M–6.9B), V5 (data and training dependence) and weakly on V7 (metric ordering).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The paraphrase should add that the emergence point is agnostic to model size. It should also add that no single data property (local dependency, categoriality, marginal shape, frequency, reliability) alone suffices for PS-measured formation.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the original prefix-matching measure, but investigates new model sizes, batch/context settings, and natural, semi-natural, and synthetic data properties rather than reproducing the original study's full method and setup.
record.method_sensitivity: Emergence timing and/or strength varies with batch size, context size, and repetition frequency. Formation varies with repetition reliability, local dependency, marginal distribution shape, and categoriality; tokenizer and corpus also change measured repetition statistics, but emergence was not tested for those combinations.

fits_no_version.finding: Final validation loss relates V-shaped (non-monotonically) to the PS emergence point across batch and context sizes. Earlier emergence helps only up to about B=64.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Timing of induction-head emergence relates non-monotonically to final LM loss under fixed compute.

record.problems: Many trajectory and grid values are available only in figures. The main natural-data configurations generally use a single random seed; the seed-robustness analysis covers six configurations and three seeds. Training is limited to up to 350M parameters, with larger Pythia models used for inference. The study does not measure token-index ICL or training-loss bumps, and the synthetic −D setup has a sampling caveat acknowledged by the authors.
record.rows_left_out: The semi-natural frequency/reliability experiment displays 60 model configurations; only the explicitly described boundary results and aggregate fitted-model result are recorded (Section 7, Figure 5). The synthetic-data cells for other conditions and the LA/AR metrics are not all separately enumerated; selected formation, absence, and boundary conditions are recorded (Section 8, Figure 6; Appendix K, Figures 15–18). Appendix L's corpus/tokenizer repetition statistics are omitted because they are proxy data properties, not model induction outcomes.

untested.parts: Entire version. No previous-token-head composition analysis, no attention-only models; PS measures only the attention pattern.
Co-occurrence with an in-context-learning score (loss vs token index) and with a training-loss bump; narrowness of the window within a run.
Families beyond GPT2/Pythia, other architectures, other modalities.
Persistence of ICL; effects of corpus and tokenizer on emergence (Appendix L only measures data repetition statistics).
Entire version; Yin & Steinhardt is only cited.
Mechanistic sub-steps of formation (e.g. previous-token head then induction head), or multiple overlapping transitions within the circuit.

missing.what: Model size is a non-significant predictor of the emergence point for all four metrics (PS p=.966, LA, AR accuracy, AR mean rank); 5-fold CV test R² mostly 0.8–0.9.
Shifting and slanting effects of batch, context and repetition replicate in LA and AR mean rank, but less clearly in AR accuracy.
Shifting effect reverses direction when emergence is plotted in tokens rather than updates.
The semi-natural decision boundary is consistent under LA. At 0.9-0.9, LA gives a weaker IH than PS; AR accuracy is more graded near the boundary.
In natural data, IHs did not form or were very weak at context size 32.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V1 'supports' label is dropped: no row measures composition or uses attention-only models. The reader's V5 'challenges' label for 0.1-0.1 is wrong: non-formation under low repetition is exactly the data dependence V5 asserts, so absent cells are part of the supporting contrast. V2 is linked only to the abruptness rows; batch/context shifting goes to V5. The −D synthetic result is metric-dependent, and the sampled data are not truly i.i.d. (authors' caveat). Most trajectory and grid values are figure-only. Main configurations use a single seed, except the six seed-robustness configurations. Original sources are not this study, so verdicts are allowed.

versions.untested_parts: Measures copying/prefix matching, but does not test composition with an earlier previous-token head or use attention-only transformers.
Measures abrupt induction-score development and its timing. Does not measure later-token loss relative to earlier tokens as ICL, or test for a training-loss bump at the same time.
Does not test whether induction heads carry most ICL in large transformers, or measure ICL by later-token loss relative to earlier tokens.
Tests GPT2 and Pythia sizes and training runs. Does not test other architectures or modalities, or broad model-family universality beyond these families.
Varies batch size, context size, repetition, and properties of synthetic training data. Does not establish how ICL persists, or test all data and training setups.
Does not compare few-shot task learning mechanisms against induction heads.
Compares timing of PS, LA, and associative-recall metrics; does not resolve whether formation comprises multiple internal mechanistic sub-steps.
